jobs.title: People Business Partner
jobs.description:
At Aceve, we back the builders of society. Founded in the Nordics and growing across Europe, we build digital tools for the people who construct and maintain our physical world - giving electricians, plumbers, and contractors back their time, clarity, and confidence. With over 900 employees across 8 countries, leading brands in 7 customer markets, and more than €100M in revenue, we're on an ambitious growth journey, and we're just getting started. We're an AI-first company, and we work with grit, openness, and a good dose of joy.

About The Job

As a People Business Partner, you'll be a trusted advisor to leaders across the organisation, helping translate business ambitions into people priorities. You'll combine strategic business partnering with hands-on execution -coaching leaders, strengthening teams, embedding our culture and making sure the fundamentals of the employee lifecycle run brilliantly.
You'll also help shape how AI becomes part of everyday work. From improving the employee experience to helping leaders build AI capabilities in their teams, you'll play an important role in making Aceve an AI-first organisation.

You can be located anywhere in the Netherlands but will be required to visit Rotterdam or Zierikzee, on a weekly basis with occasional travel across Europe.

Your role is all about our brilliant people, and your focus will be to;

Partner with leaders to strengthen performance, organisational capability and team effectiveness.
Coach leaders on performance, change, employee relations and leadership development.
Drive the implementation of Aceve's culture and values across the organisation.
Help build our AI-first way of working by driving adoption, capability and smarter ways of working.
Own and continuously improve the employee lifecycle, from onboarding to development, performance and offboarding.
Use people data and insights to support better business decisions.
Deliver practical, business-focused people support while ensuring compliance with Dutch labour legislation.
Collaborate with the People & Culture team to build scalable people practices across Europe.

Who are you?

You're curious about business and passionate about people. You enjoy thinking strategically but get just as much satisfaction from rolling up your sleeves and making things happen.
You build trust through credibility, humility and collaboration. You coach leaders with confidence, challenge when needed and know that great People Partners spend time in the business -not just behind a screen.
You already use AI to work smarter and are excited about helping others do the same. You believe technology should make work better, not more complicated.

You'll Probably Bring

Experience as a People Business Partner in a fast-paced, international environment.
Strong leadership coaching and stakeholder management skills.
Experience across the employee lifecycle and organisational development.
A data-informed approach to decision-making.
AI literacy and a genuine curiosity about how AI can improve the way we work.
Knowledge of Dutch labour law.
Fluency in English. Dutch is a plus.

Why Aceve?

Shape the future of a growing European SaaS company.
Help build an AI-first organisation where people and technology grow together.
Work with talented colleagues across Europe in a collaborative, down-to-earth culture.
Enjoy real ownership, influence and the opportunity to make a visible impact from day one.

Not ticking every box?
No worries! We value potential and drive, so apply anyway or connect
with us- you might be just what we're looking for in our growing organisation! Join Aceve and take your expertise to the next level, together we are redefining what’s possible in craft and construction solutions!

Aceve is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Our selection process is conducted continuously and without discrimination, ensuring an equal opportunity for all candidates.

Description

What does it mean to be a part of the Escalon team?

For nearly two decades Escalon has helped more than 5,000 companies across a range of industries to optimize their back-office processes. At Escalon, we deliver Essential Business Services to organizations so that owners and leaders can focus on the core of their business while Escalon takes care of the rest. Escalon’s simple and intuitive technology and outsourcing solutions significantly reduce the administrative costs and time needed to perform FinOps, PeopleOps, and Risk “back-office” services. “And done” is our simple way to describe how we deliver high-quality, exceptional service to our clients.

We’re looking for motivated and goal-driven team members who can do what it takes to make a company great. The reward is an exciting, flexible and creative environment with opportunities for professional and personal growth. As our name indicates, working at Escalon is taking the step on the ladder to long-term career growth and ultimately meeting your personal career goals.

Partner with Payroll team and oversee the implementation and/or process payroll processing for multiple clients in a timely manner and assist employees with questions.
Leave of Absence:
Partner with clients to draft parental leave policies and customize and deliver each employee LOA packet, support employee questions, and ensure leave is compliant based on local, state, and federal laws.
Employee Relations:
Recommend, implement, and support clients with feedback process, and support employee relations questions, demands, grievances, or other issues.
Performance Management
: Assess needs and provide recommendation to design, customize, and implement performance management selection and processes, ensuring all employees receive timely and actionable feedback for applicable clients.

Assess, recommend, and develop programs designed to enhance employee morale and productivity, and recognize employees for their contributions to the company’s success. Assist with preventing and resolving concerns. Collaborate with managers to resolve issues and assist to prepare corrective action.

What You’ll Bring:

Must Haves:
Must have 3+ years of human resources/people operations experience
Experience scaling and supporting venture and/or private equity backed companies preferred
Must have knowledge of startup HR best practices, while thriving in an entrepreneurial environment
Strong business acumen and a passion for HR; people-oriented and results driven
Must have exceptional knowledge of local, state, and federal employment laws
Ability to exercise autonomy, independent judgment, and decision making; providing sound recommendation to clients to resolve issues and mitigate risk while providing excellent client delivery
Ability to handle pressure and manage multiple projects with frequently changing priorities, and possess an eye for detail
Professional demeanor and excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
Strong interpersonal skills, high level of professionalism and integrity
Ability to professionally handle confidential data and information
Self-motivated, with a strong work ethic and demonstrated initiative with a sense of urgency
Knowledge of HRIS, Payroll and Recruiting systems (Gusto, Zenefits, Namely, Rippling, ADP, Paychex, Paylocity, Intuit, TriNet, Justworks, Sequoia, Greenhouse, Lever, etc.)

Nice to Haves:
Bachelor’s degree and/or PHR certification preferred.
Experience with Mergers & Acquisitions and best practices & processes are preferred.

A hands-on, high-execution role at the heart of our people’s function.

This position plays a key role in running day-to-day HR operations while contributing to Teladoc Health's people strategy in Amsterdam as we scale.

Teladoc Health is looking for a hands-on HR Manager to take ownership of People Operations in the Netherlands. In this broad and autonomous role, you will ensure that our HR operations, recruitment and employee processes run smoothly, while acting as a trusted people partner to the Country Manager and local Management Team.

You will be the primary HR contact for employees in the Netherlands and work closely with colleagues in our regional and global People & Culture organization. Your initial focus will be on operational excellence, Dutch employment-law compliance, recruitment and employee experience. As the local HR foundation develops, you will also contribute to workforce planning, organizational development and other strategic people priorities.

Own end-to-end HR operations: contracts, onboarding, offboarding, payroll coordination, benefits administration, and employee records

Advise the Country Manager and local Management Team on people, organization and employment matters.

Maintain accurate HR systems, trackers, and reporting so leadership always has an up-to-date picture of the team

Contribute to strategic people topics as they arise, including workforce planning, compensation benchmarking, and org design input, while keeping operational delivery as the day-to-day priority

Essential: high execution power, approachable and easy-going manners, pragmatism, clear communication, with strong judgement, ownership, discretion, the ability to set priorities independently, and eagerness to grow with the company

jobs.title: People and Culture Specialist
jobs.description:
Modern Family Law, a boutique law firm which specializes in Family Law, is looking for a compassionate, innovative, and organized People & Culture Specialist - Employee Relations, Leave and Accommodations
to work remotely near one of our office locations. Modern Family Law offers dynamic compensation, a wide array of benefit selections, and a culture built on family.

Role Summary

The People & Culture Specialist leads day-to-day employee relations, leave, and accommodation work for the Firm's multi-state workforce. The role is a primary partner to managers, Managing Attorneys (MAs), and employees on workplace concerns, performance and conduct matters, and leave or accommodation requests. The specialist owns assigned matters from intake through resolution, communicates clear recommendations, documents decisions and follow-up, and leads approved People & Culture initiatives through implementation. The role works independently within established policies and guidance and promptly brings significant legal, employee, or policy risk to People & Culture leadership.

Responsibilities

Lead the day-to-day employee relations process for assigned matters, including intake, issue assessment, fact-finding, interviews, investigations, findings, recommendations, communication, documentation, and follow-up.
Serve as a trusted People & Culture partner to MAs, managers, and employees. Lead consultations and meetings, clarify the concern, coach managers on fair and consistent next steps, and confirm agreed actions are completed.
Advise managers on performance, conduct, attendance, workplace conflict, retention, and other employee concerns. Promote coaching and development where appropriate and partner with P&C leadership on formal corrective action or separation decisions.
Use sound judgment to resolve routine matters within Firm policy. Escalate promptly to P&C leadership any allegation or circumstance involving significant legal or employee risk, potential retaliation or discrimination, safety concerns, policy interpretation or exceptions, or a proposed high-impact employment decision.
Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential case records, including relevant facts, analysis, recommendations, decisions, communications, and assigned follow-up. Track open actions and deadlines through completion.
Own assigned leave and accommodation matters, including applicable ADA, FMLA, state and local leave laws, and religious accommodations. Coordinate the interactive process, required documentation, employee and manager communication, and timely case milestones.
Partner with employees, managers, payroll, benefits, and other stakeholders to coordinate leave administration and workplace accommodations while protecting confidential medical information and limiting access to those with a business need.
Monitor changes in employment and leave requirements across the Firm's jurisdictions. Research questions, identify operational impacts, recommend updates, and support implementation of policies, procedures, handbook materials, and manager guidance.
Lead approved employee relations, leave, accommodation, and employee experience initiatives from planning through completion. Define deliverables and milestones, coordinate owners, communicate status and risks, resolve routine blockers, and confirm adoption and follow-through.
Develop, document, and maintain practical procedures, templates, and process guides that improve consistency, timely handling, compliance, and scalability across the Firm.
Review case and leave data, recurring themes, and manager feedback to identify trends and recommend specific actions to P&C leadership. Track agreed actions and report progress and outcomes.
Partner with P&C leadership to plan and deliver manager education and resources on employee relations, performance conversations, leave, accommodations, and effective partnership with P&C. Follow up on questions and reinforce key practices.
Work with cross-functional partners to resolve employee matters and implement People & Culture processes. Keep stakeholders informed of their responsibilities, timelines, and next steps.
Perform other related duties as assigned to support People & Culture and Firm needs.

Requirements

Requirements

At least six (5) years of progressively responsible experience in employee relations, human resources, leave administration, accommodations, employment compliance, or a closely related field, including independent ownership of complex matters and projects.
A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, or a related field is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience will be considered.
Demonstrated experience conducting employee relations reviews or investigations and advising managers on performance, conduct, workplace concerns, and appropriate follow-up.
Hands-on experience administering leave and accommodation processes, including the ADA, FMLA, and applicable state and local requirements.
Working knowledge of employment practices and multi-state requirements, including California, Colorado, Texas, Washington, Virginia and Georgia; ability to research and apply requirements in additional jurisdictions as the Firm expands.
Experience in a law firm, professional services, or a rapidly growing multi-state organization is preferred.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Outlook, SharePoint, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as Adobe, Slack, and Zoom.
Reliable remote work setup, including high-speed internet and a functional workstation.

Skills And Competencies

Takes initiative and follows work through to completion; translates broad goals into clear deliverables, milestones, ownership, and regular updates.
Exercises sound judgment, balances employee care with consistent policy application, and knows when to consult or escalate.
Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills, interacting with employees, MAs, managers, and leaders at all levels with professionalism, empathy, and clarity through phone, video, email, and messaging platforms.
Organizes multiple sensitive matters effectively, prioritizes deadlines, and maintains reliable documentation and follow-up.
Builds trust while handling confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Uses facts and available data to identify patterns, explain options, and make practical recommendations.
Works independently with minimal supervision while collaborating effectively across teams and adapting to changing business needs.

Benefits

ADA Compliance:
Candidates must be able to perform the role's duties with or without reasonable accommodations. Requests for accommodations should be made to the Director of People Operations in advance.

Compensation and Benefits: Salary Range for California and Washington: $95,000-$105,000. This range is a reasonably reliable estimate of the base salary that this role is expected to receive.
Actual pay will be adjusted based on experience, location, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

Comprehensive benefits package includes health insurance, HSA/FSA options, short-term and long-term disability, dental and vision care, life insurance, 401(k), vacation, sick time, and access to an employee assistance program. Additional voluntary benefits include accident insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, critical illness insurance, long-term care insurance, and pet insurance. Commuter and transit benefits may be available in some locations.

Business Acumen — understands how the organization makes money and frames people decisions in those terms.

Partner with employees, managers, payroll, benefits, and other stakeholders to coordinate leave administration and workplace accommodations while protecting confidential medical information and limiting access to those with a business need.
Monitor changes in employment and leave requirements across the Firm's jurisdictions. Research questions, identify operational impacts, recommend updates, and support implementation of policies, procedures, handbook materials, and manager guidance.

Requirements

Demonstrated experience conducting employee relations reviews or investigations and advising managers on performance, conduct, workplace concerns, and appropriate follow-up.
Hands-on experience administering leave and accommodation processes, including the ADA, FMLA, and applicable state and local requirements.
Working knowledge of employment practices and multi-state requirements, including California, Colorado, Texas, Washington, Virginia and Georgia; ability to research and apply requirements in additional jurisdictions as the Firm expands.
Experience in a law firm, professional services, or a rapidly growing multi-state organization is preferred.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Outlook, SharePoint, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as Adobe, Slack, and Zoom.
Reliable remote work setup, including high-speed internet and a functional workstation.

Takes initiative and follows work through to completion; translates broad goals into clear deliverables, milestones, ownership, and regular updates.

Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills, interacting with employees, MAs, managers, and leaders at all levels with professionalism, empathy, and clarity through phone, video, email, and messaging platforms.

Works independently with minimal supervision while collaborating effectively across teams and adapting to changing business needs.

new_jobs.title: Sr Manager, HRBP's - North America
new_jobs.description:
The Senior Manager, HR Business Partners – North America leads the HRBP function across the United States and Canada, serving as both a people leader and a senior business partner to executive stakeholders. This is a player-coach role: you will manage and develop a team of HR Business Partners while personally owning partnership with one or more senior client groups.

You will translate business strategy into people strategy — shaping organizational design, talent planning, leadership capability, employee relations practice, and engagement across the region. You will act as the connective tissue between the business and the HR Centers of Excellence (Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Talent Development, HR Operations), ensuring that regional execution is consistent, compliant, and commercially relevant.

Success in this role is measured by the quality of leadership decisions your team enables, the health of the organizations you support, and the credibility the HRBP function holds with the business.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership

Serve as the senior HR partner to designated executive leaders in the US and Canada, contributing to business planning and acting as a trusted advisor on all people matters.
Translate business objectives into an actionable regional people agenda covering talent, structure, capability, culture, and cost.
Use workforce data and business metrics to identify trends, diagnose root causes, and recommend interventions rather than react to symptoms.
Provide coaching and candid counsel to senior leaders on leadership effectiveness, team dynamics, decision-making, and change.

Team Leadership and Development

Lead, coach, and develop a team of HR Business Partners supporting client groups across North America; set clear expectations, priorities, and standards of practice.
Build team capability in consulting skills, data fluency, employee relations judgment, and commercial understanding.
Allocate HRBP coverage and workload across the region, balancing client demand with development opportunities for the team.
Manage team performance, conduct regular one-to-ones and performance reviews, and build succession depth within the function.
Model the standards of partnership, confidentiality, and professionalism expected of the function.

Talent, Organization, and Change

Lead organizational design and workforce planning activity for client groups, including restructures, role design, spans and layers, and location strategy.
Drive talent review, succession planning, and calibration cycles across North America; ensure clear action follows assessment.
Partner with Talent Acquisition on critical hires, internal mobility, and leadership selection.
Lead HR delivery on change programs — integrations, reorganizations, site openings and closures — including impact assessment, consultation, and communication planning.

Employee Relations and Compliance

Own the standard of employee relations practice across the region; oversee complex investigations, performance management, accommodation, and separation matters.
Ensure consistency, fairness, and defensible documentation in all ER outcomes; escalate and partner with Legal where appropriate.
Maintain compliance with US and Canadian federal, state, and provincial employment law (including FLSA, FMLA, ADA, Title VII, state leave and pay transparency requirements, provincial employment standards, and human rights legislation).
Review and localize HR policy for North America in partnership with Legal and global HR; drive consistent application across the region.

Performance, Engagement, and Culture

Drive the annual performance and compensation cycles for client groups in partnership with Total Rewards, including calibration, merit, and promotion decisions.
Interpret engagement and listening data for the region; work with leaders to convert insight into sustained action.
Champion inclusion, wellbeing, and a consistent employee experience across US and Canadian locations.

Operational Excellence

Partner with HR Operations to ensure accurate employee data, clean processes, and an effective service model across the region.
Define and track HRBP metrics — attrition, time to fill, internal mobility, ER cycle time, engagement — and report on regional people performance to leadership.
Identify and remove low-value activity from the HRBP team’s workload through process improvement, manager enablement, and self-service.
Manage regional HR budget items within area of responsibility.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 5 years in an HR Business Partner or generalist role supporting senior leaders.
Demonstrated experience partnering at the executive level, including influencing decisions you do not control.
Working knowledge of US employment law and practice; working knowledge of Canadian employment standards and human rights legislation, or demonstrated ability to acquire it quickly.
Proven track record leading complex employee relations matters and organizational change.
Strong analytical capability — comfortable building a case with workforce data and presenting it to a commercial audience.
Experience working in a matrixed, multi-site environment.

Preferred

2+ years of direct people management experience leading HR professionals preferred but not required.
SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or CHRL/CHRP certification.
Experience supporting both the US and Canada within a single regional remit.
Experience with HRIS platforms (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, or similar) and HR analytics tooling.
Experience supporting organizations through M&A integration.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Business Acumen — understands how the organization makes money and frames people decisions in those terms.
Influence and Credibility — earns a seat at the table through judgment and delivery, not title; comfortable delivering unwelcome advice.
Coaching and Development — raises the capability of both direct reports and the leaders they support.
Judgment Under Ambiguity — makes sound, defensible decisions in sensitive situations with incomplete information.
Data Fluency — interrogates workforce data, identifies the real pattern, and communicates it clearly.
Change Leadership — plans, sequences, and lands organizational change with the human impact managed deliberately.
Operating Discipline — runs a consistent, well-documented practice across multiple countries and client groups.
Integrity and Discretion — holds confidence absolutely and applies standards evenly regardless of seniority.
